name: brine-theme
description: Dark monochrome theme for the Pterodactyl Panel user area - #0b0b0d page, #141417 surfaces, #c8ccd0 neutral accent, fixed sidebar shell, redesigned dashboard, login, account, console and file manager. Admin area, favicon and page title untouched.

files.note: Deleted. It keyed an uploaded illustration's white background to transparency and cropped it, which existed only for the hero illustration in the 50/50 auth split. Both are gone, so the class has no caller. Listed with action `remove` rather than simply dropped from the manifest, because a panel that installed an earlier version still has the file on disk and would otherwise be left with an orphan that no installer run could clean up. Both installers back the panel's copy up before deleting it, so uninstall restores it

Dropdown positioning and surface. The stock panel rendered `absolute` inside a plain wrapper and nudged it with `left = viewportX - width`, which is only correct when the wrapper sits at the viewport origin - inside a .file_row it was pushed off to the right, and the row clipped it, so the per-file actions never appeared. Now `position: fixed` with the vertical placement taken from the toggle rect and clamped to the viewport, repositioned on scroll/resize. Surface uses the theme tokens instead of bg-white. Same props, named export and triggerMenu ref API as stock

Stock Field plus two additive props. `labelAction` renders on the label row beside the label, which the reference needs for "Forgot password?". `label` is widened from string to ReactNode so a caller can mark a field required with a styled asterisk - the register screen does this on all six of its fields. Both additive: with neither prop the markup is byte-for-byte what stock produced, so the panel's other ~200 Field call sites are untouched

Per-file actions panel. The stock rows hovered to bg-neutral-100 on text-neutral-700, which on the black palette is a near-white bar with near-black text across a dark menu; rows are now tinted to the palette so hover brightens by one step and Delete reads as destructive without turning white. Toggle matches the file-row hover and names the file for screen readers. Same behaviour as stock, including the pterodactyl:files:ctx right-click event

Emits every colour utility as rgb(var(--pt-*)) on Tailwind 3.1+ and as baked-in hex on 2.1/3.0, which cannot apply an opacity modifier to a CSS variable; adds navy/gold brand ramps and aliases blue/primary to navy and cyan to gold. The literal PALETTE here is the pre-3.1 fallback and MUST stay byte-for-byte in step with the --pt-* blocks in pterodactyl-theme.css: it is the only palette a panel on Tailwind below 3.1 ever sees, so drift there renders the old colours while the stylesheet declares the new ones - which is indistinguishable from the stylesheet not having applied. The default palette is now light (page #f2f4f6, card #ffffff, dark ink, blue accent) and the ramp keeps its roles across that flip, 50-500 ink and 600-900 surfaces, so the stock panel utilities follow without touching a component

Stock head (title, csrf, robots) + the theme favicon only, plus data-pt-theme on <html> and a theme-color that follows the chosen palette - both server-rendered so a variant never shows the default for a frame. The stylesheet is cache-busted on its own mtime: config(app.version) is the panel version, so it never changes on a theme update and browsers kept the previous stylesheet for the max-age the server sends. The favicon picks the newest custom-logo.* and appends its mtime, and the icon MIME type comes from the extension rather than being hardcoded to image/png
ptColor() helper for Chart.js - dark-only, no theme state

The server routes the theme adds on top of the panel routes.server table - Plugins and Mods - in one place so the router, the sidebar and the topbar title cannot drift apart. Each carries a jarKind that gates its nav item

brandName()/logoUrl()/registrationEnabled()/backgroundStyle()/quickLinks()/linkHref()/socialProviders()/socialRedirectUrl()/accountAccess() - site name, icon, the registration switch, the two background slots, the Home/Discord/Status links, the enabled social providers and what this session may change about itself, all from window.SiteConfiguration. socialProviders() only ever sees an id and a label: the OAuth client secret stays server-side and never reaches the browser. accountAccess() reports AssetComposer's account.can_change_email and resolves signed_in_with to a provider label through socialProviders() rather than keeping a second copy of the names here; it defaults to the CLOSED state, because a panel still running the previous AssetComposer has no account key at all and offering a button that will be refused is worse than offering none

Light tokens (#f2f4f6 page, #ffffff cards, dark ink, system fonts) plus the dark chrome islands the reference shell is built from - a slate topbar and slate server cards floating on the white page, each with its own light ink steps, because the page ink is unreadable on them. The neutral ramp keeps its ROLES across the polarity flip (50-500 ink, 600-900 surfaces), which is what lets the stock panel ~200 colour utilities re-skin with no component edits; the console header is a third island for the same reason. That flip also breaks the panel's own PAIRED Tailwind colours, and there is one rule here for the case that bit: the copy toast is emitted as `text-gray-200 bg-neutral-600/95`, a matched pair on stock that this ramp turns into dark ink on a light surface - i.e. invisible - so the exact class COMBINATION is overridden rather than either half, because `text-gray-200` alone is correct all over the panel. Every pairing is measured rather than eyeballed: stock muted ink clears 4.5:1 on both the page and a card, and the blue fill clears 4.57:1 with white text. Also owns the app shell - a topbar-only shell with a mobile drawer, plus a fixed desktop rail on SERVER pages only, which starts below the topbar through --pt-topbar-h rather than a literal 4rem repeated in two rules, and which offsets .pt-shell-main and never .pt-shell-body because the topbar is a direct child of the body - the centred dashboard with its two-column card grid, admin-set background image layers with an adjustable scrim, the auth screens, the account screens, and the server status panel. .pt-topbar is deliberately NOT in the radii opt-in list: a full-width bar with rounded corners floats above the page with a notch at each end, which next to the rail beneath reads as the header being inset from its own navigation. Defines --pt-font-mono, which two rules were already referencing without it existing - an undefined custom property is not a CSS error, it silently inherits, which is how the file manager's monospace path bar came to render in the panel's sans-serif. Keeps the amber palette as a dark-gold [data-pt-theme] alternative, shared scale tokens (shadow/hairline/duration), the squaring reset and its opt-in lists, and the reduced-motion / reduced-transparency / forced-colors blocks
Brand mark used by the sidebar and the login screen

Deleted. It only ever rendered the admin's Home/Discord/Status links as pill clusters - <TopbarLinkCluster> in the dashboard topbar and, before that, <AuthLinks> on the auth screens. Both are gone, so the component has no caller. The links themselves are untouched and still work: Admin -> Site Settings -> Links still stores them, lib/brand.ts still exposes quickLinks() and linkHref(), and AuthenticationRouter still uses linkHref('home') for the auth breadcrumb and footer. Only the dashboard stopped rendering them, because that cluster is what forced the topbar into a 1fr auto 1fr grid with an empty balancing column, which squeezed the right-hand cluster until the sign-out button was clipped. Listed with action `remove` rather than dropped from the manifest so a panel that installed an earlier version gets the orphaned file cleaned up instead of being left with a dead component webpack can still pull in

Topbar + mobile drawer shell for dashboard and server routes; applies the dashboard background image. On the dashboard and account pages there is still no desktop sidebar - the reference shell is a topbar only, and the navigation that lived in the sidebar moved into NavigationBar as icon-over-label items; the drawer keeps the full navigation on narrow screens. ON SERVER PAGES a fixed left rail is back, from lg up, because a server page has ten destinations plus the theme's own Plugins and Mods and two topbar icons cannot hold that without hiding them. It is rendered here rather than in ServerRouter so `mode` stays the single thing that decides the shell and the drawer and the rail cannot disagree. The rail is always in the DOM and hidden below lg with CSS so a resize across the breakpoint mounts nothing, and is aria-hidden there because the drawer is the real navigation at those widths and two navigations for one page is a screen reader reading the same list twice. The rail's offset is applied to `.pt-shell-main`, never to `.pt-shell-body`: NavigationBar renders the topbar as a direct child of the body, so padding the body pushed the header sideways too and left a 15rem white hole in the top-left corner above the rail. The account page title also resolves through lib/accountRoutes.ts, for the reason the server one does: /account/email is a theme route, so it is not in routes.account and the fallback would title it 'Account'

The panel navigation list, used twice: in the mobile drawer on every page, and in the fixed desktop rail on server pages. Brand block, permission-filtered server entries, account entries, the admin shortcut, and a footer with the avatar and sign-out - but the frame around it depends on `variant`. 'drawer' is the mobile one: brand on top, footer at the bottom. 'rail' is the desktop column on a server page, which the reference shapes differently: the server's own identity sits at the top (name, short identifier, and a dot carrying the power state) and there is no brand block or footer, because the topbar directly above carries the logo and the avatar. Two variants rather than two components on purpose - the NAVIGATION is one list and must stay one list, or the rail and the drawer drift into offering different destinations; only the frame changes. The rail's server identity arrives as PROPS, not as ServerContext hooks, and that is a correction rather than a style choice: AppShell renders this component for the mobile drawer on every page, while App.tsx mounts ServerContext.Provider only around /server/:id, so a hook here throws on / and /account and the panel's ErrorBoundary replaces the whole dashboard with 'An error was encountered by the application while rendering this view'. That is a CLIENT-side render error and never reaches the Laravel log, so a log check finds nothing. Account entries are built from the panel's routes.account with the theme's own appended, both compared through normalizeAccountPath() so the two spellings of the overview cannot produce a duplicate. The theme's Email Address item renders only when accountAccess() allows it, because a nav entry that leads to a refusal is worse than no entry

Topbar-only navigation shell. Three-column grid (1fr auto 1fr): pt-topbar-lead carries the burger, the brand lockup and a quiet page-title line; the centre column is the Home/Discord/Status pill cluster; pt-topbar-tail carries icon-over-label Servers and Account links, the Admin shortcut for a root admin, the username with a Logout button beneath it, and the round avatar. It replaced a title-only bar once the fixed sidebar was removed to match the reference shell - the navigation that lived in the sidebar moved here. onLogout is a prop rather than an inlined POST because AppShell owns http(). The burger and mobile drawer are unchanged: a phone still reaches the full navigation through the drawer, so removing the desktop sidebar was a layout change and not a loss of nav. The page title is kept beside the brand rather than dropped, because on a server page it is the only thing naming which server you are in

Wraps server routes in AppShell and drops the legacy SubNavigation, and mounts the theme own server routes (Plugins and Mods) after the panel table so a stock route of the same path would win rather than be shadowed

Auth routes: adds /auth/register, applies the auth background image, and owns the page chrome that frames every auth screen - a top bar (brand lockup left, Home / <screen> breadcrumb right, current screen in the accent with an underline) and a bottom bar (credit left, Home + Login right). The form centres in the space between them via .pt-auth-body. The breadcrumb used to be absolutely positioned into the page's top-left corner, which is where the reference puts its logo; the logo is now the bar lockup and the breadcrumb sits opposite it. The bottom bar's credit reads "Designed by BrineAjay" - a hardcoded theme credit, not a setting

The auth shell shared by every auth screen: a single flat column on a dark page - emblem centred above the heading, then the optional social sign-in row, then the sign-up call to action, then the form directly on the page with no card. This replaced a 50/50 split whose left half existed to carry a hero illustration, and then replaced the white form card, which the reference has no equivalent of. The logo moved off the top-left corner (where the breadcrumb lives) and lost its brand-name text, since the heading already reads "Welcome to <brand>". The sign-up CTA renders only when registration is actually enabled, so it can never link to a route the admin has closed, and showSignUpCta=false turns it off on the register screen where the footer already offers the same link. `social` is a slot rather than an imported component, so this shared shell does not decide that login has social buttons and register might not - each screen passes its own instance or omits the prop and the row is simply absent

Login form + success flash after registration (?registered=1) + error flash after a failed social sign-in (?social_error=). Matches the reference's arrangement: "Welcome to <brand>" heading, the social row, full-width sign-up CTA, "or", then one small "Login" label above a single row holding username, password and the submit button side by side, with "Forgot password?" under the row. The per-field labels are still rendered but clipped (not display:none) so they stay in the accessibility tree - a placeholder is not a label. The field stays "Username or Email" because the endpoint accepts either. Both "you came back here with a message" cases are handled in ONE mount effect: clearFlashes() runs first so a stale error never carries over from the previous page, then at most one branch fires, and since the first branch already called replaceState the second cannot read a rewritten URL. The card the form used to sit in is still deliberately absent. The "Want to manage a friend's server?" subuser nudge was removed earlier (component, prop, caller, CSS and preview all dropped together)

Public registration form (email, first/last name, username, password, confirm) posting to /auth/register. Matches the reference: heading split so 'your account' takes the accent colour, a leading glyph on every field, a placeholder on every field, blue asterisk on every label (all six are `.required()` in the schema below the markup), and first/last name sharing a row. Layout moved off twin.macro margins onto .pt-auth-stack / .pt-auth-pair, so the spacing is a gap the stylesheet owns. Also renders the social sign-in row: signing up with a provider creates the account directly, so the password fields below are not the only way in and the row belongs here as much as on the login form
CSRF + POST /auth/register client
Same treatment for the 2FA checkpoint screen
Same treatment for the password recovery screen
Same treatment for the password recovery screen, including the same corrected muted-link hover direction

The two pieces both account screens share: the dark chrome card with its title, a real ? toggle and the help panel it reveals, and the labelled control inside it (label above, then one light box holding a glyph and the input side by side). They are their own file rather than duplicated per container because the change-email page is a second form built from exactly these parts - two copies is how the two pages drift a shade apart while both claim to be the reference's account screen. The fields are hand-written rather than built on the panel's Field/Input for the reason given on AccountOverviewContainer. Also exports AccountReadonly, which shows the current address as text rather than a disabled <input>: a disabled field is skipped by tab order, is announced as unlabelled text by some screen readers, and this one is never submitted

The change-email page (/account/email): the address the account has now, then New Email, Confirm New Email and - last, on purpose - the current password that gates the change. The password is the whole point: changing the address is how an account is taken over and the panel does not confirm it with a second factor. A session opened with Google or Discord is shown the reason and a way back instead of a form it could never satisfy - an account created through a provider holds a 48-character random password nobody was told (createFromProfile stores one only because the column is NOT NULL), so there is nothing to type into a 'current password' box. Refusals from the endpoint are attached to the field they are about (errors[0].meta.field) and stay put, because Formik drops its own errors on the next keystroke and 'that is not your current password' has to remain readable; anything without a field goes to the flash. The address readout is state, not a read at render, so a save updates it without a reload - the panel rewrites window.PterodactylUser only on a full page load and the session guard resolves the user per request, so there is no cached copy to refresh

Account routes the theme adds on top of the panel's routes.account table, in one place so DashboardRouter and AppShell cannot drift apart - the same arrangement as serverExtras.ts for the server routes. Exports normalizeAccountPath() because the two tables do not spell the overview the same way: the panel uses '/' where the theme uses ''. That is not cosmetic - a literal comparison MISSED the panel's own overview entry, which resolves to /account/, so the panel's account component stayed in the bundle for a page it could never render

PUT /auth/account/email - change the address on the signed-in account. A theme endpoint rather than the panel's PUT /api/client/account/email because the rule this feature needs has nowhere to live on the panel's route: routes/api-client.php is a panel file the theme does not ship, so no middleware can be attached to it, and the panel has no concept of a social session to hang the rule on anyway. Hiding the button would have been the whole of the enforcement, and hiding a button is not a check. The WRITE is still the panel's - UserUpdateService, the model's own getRulesForUpdate() rules (rather than a copy of them, which is how the unique rule ends up wrongly rewritten to not ignore this row and a saved address that never changed comes back as 'already taken'), the panel's own 3-per-24h email budget on the panel's own rate-limit key so the two paths share one allowance, and the user:account.email-changed activity log. Checks in this order, and the first one is first on purpose: a session that may not make this change must not be able to use it to test whether a password is correct either. Hash::check is the panel's own call and returns false rather than throwing for an unreadable hash, which is where a provider-created account's unknown password turns into a refusal instead of an exception. Every refusal is the panel's errors[0].detail shape, because httpErrorToHuman() reads that and a bare Laravel 422 arrives at the form as 'Request failed with status code 422'

The account page (/account), rebuilt in the theme as a dark chrome card on the light page, matching the server-card idiom: a header (title + a real ? toggle that reveals a help panel), three labelled fields and a green confirm. Posts to the panel's own /api/client/account/password, so the current password is verified and the new one hashed by the panel - no custom auth. The card and the fields now come from AccountCard.tsx, shared with the change-email page. Adds the GREEN Change Email button under Update Password, opening /account/email - a Link rather than a button with an onClick, so middle-click, open-in-new-tab and copy-link keep working, and an anchor cannot submit the surrounding form by accident. A session opened with Google or Discord gets a sentence in its place rather than the button: such an account has no password its owner was ever given, so the form could only ever end in a refusal, and offering it would be offering a dead end. That is a UI decision, not the enforcement - AssetComposer decides it and AccountEmailController re-checks it. The other account screens (API credentials, SSH keys, activity) are still reachable: the panel's /account/* sub-routes still render the panel's own components

POST /api/client/account/password and PUT /auth/account/email. The password change is the panel's own client endpoint, so it needs no sanctum/csrf-cookie priming (that is what api/auth/register.ts does, and only because its endpoint is a web route); the email change is the theme's own WEB route, so it primes for the same reason register.ts does. Both go through the panel's shared http instance to keep the session cookie, the X-XSRF header and the panel's error shape. The email wire names are the theme endpoint's and are NOT the panel's client API names - it reads the current password from `password` and the new address from `email`, whereas the panel's own email endpoint reads `current_password`; sending the wrong one is a 403 about a password that was never supplied. readEmailError() reads errors[0].detail with errors[0].meta.field as the field hint, so a wrong password lands under the right input instead of only in a toast

Wraps the dashboard in AppShell, drops the legacy SubNavigation, and routes /account and /account/email to the theme's own components. The panel's routes.account list is NOT overridden wholesale - it is also what the drawer's navigation reads, so replacing it would change that list too. Instead the entries the theme provides are filtered OUT of the map and routed explicitly. Filtering rather than relying on route order: the map's own entries resolve to the same URLs, and two routes for one URL is a thing that breaks the moment the order changes. Both tables are compared through normalizeAccountPath() because they spell the overview differently (panel '/', theme ''), and the previous literal `path !== ''` comparison therefore never filtered the panel's own overview - it resolved to /account/, was shadowed by the theme's /account, and left the panel's component in the bundle for a page it could not render

GET /auth/servers/eggs - the egg NAME for every server the caller can see, so the dashboard card can label a server by its software. The panel cannot answer this on the servers list: ServerTransformer returns neither an egg name nor an egg id (egg_features is the only egg-derived field, and it is identical across the Minecraft eggs), and the egg relationship needs an explicit ?include=egg that ServerController::index never asks for. A family can be guessed from the egg's variable names and the theme does guess one, but Paper, Spigot and Purpur are indistinguishable that way, so the NAME has to come from the server. Lives under Auth purely because that is the only web route file the theme ships that a normal user can reach - routes/admin.php is behind AdminAuthenticate, and base.php and api-client.php are panel files the theme does not ship; the route strips the `guest` middleware auth.php is mounted under and adds `auth`, as the logout route and /auth/account/email do. Scoped by the panel's own accessibleServers() relation (the one behind the server switcher), so owner, subuser and admin access resolve through the panel's rules rather than a hand-written join; a root admin gets all of them, which reveals nothing new since Admin -> Servers already shows each server's egg, and without it the dashboard's show-all-servers switch would leave every other admin's card on a guess. A server with no egg comes back as an explicit null rather than being omitted, so the client can tell 'really has no egg' from 'no idea about this server' and pick its fallback accordingly

GET /auth/servers/eggs client. One request per dashboard load, not one per card: the endpoint returns every server the caller can see, so 40 servers still make one call. A null VALUE is a visible server with no egg; an absent KEY is a server this caller cannot see, which happens for a non-root admin looking at another admin's server with show-all-servers on. No sanctum/csrf-cookie priming, unlike the POST/PUT endpoints beside it - this is a GET, so VerifyCsrfToken does not inspect it

The dashboard in the reference shape: a centred blue Servers title with a quiet greeting line, a row carrying the admin-only show-all-servers switch on the left and the Create button on the right, then a two-column grid of server cards. The previous branded hero block and section title are gone - .pt-dash-title replaces both - but firstName is still read and shown, because dropping the user name would lose something the layout change did not require. Also fetches the egg names through its own useSWR, on a separate key from the server list: the map is not paginated and does not change when the page or the show-all-servers switch does, so switching pages or filters does not refetch it. It is deliberately never awaited and never fed to the flash - a card that cannot name its software still has to render, via ServerRow's family and node fallbacks, so an endpoint failure must not take the dashboard down with it

One server as a card in the reference grid: pink left accent bar, name, uuid, software, and a round power button that is pink to stop and blue to start. This replaced a full-width row carrying live CPU/memory/disk bars and status/allocation chips - the bars were why a scrolling list of these was expensive to render and why it read as a data table rather than a list of servers, and the numbers are one click away on the server page. Still a single Link, so the power button stops propagation. The press is optimistic and rolls back if the daemon refuses it; suspended and node-maintenance servers are not polled at all. The third line is the egg NAME, passed in as `eggName` from DashboardContainer's single /auth/servers/eggs request, because the panel does not send it on the servers list: ServerTransformer returns neither a name nor an id, and the egg relationship needs ?include=egg, which ServerController::index never requests. The card used to read server.eggName || server.egg and print 'No egg assigned' when both were missing - which was ALWAYS, so every server displayed it, Paper servers included. Before that request lands it falls back to serverFamilyLabel(server.variables), a coarser but real answer, and then to server.node, which the transformer always sends; that last fallback is not theoretical, since includeVariables() returns a NULL RESOURCE (not an empty one) for a subuser without ACTION_STARTUP_READ. The power call goes through the shared `@/api/http` client rather than a per-server panel module: `@/api/server/sendPowerAction` is absent on some panel versions in this theme's supported range, and importing it was a build-time Module not found error rather than a runtime one. `http` is already imported by AppShell and ServerRouter, so it resolves wherever the theme builds at all
Adds the shared footer: Powered by the panel's own site name via brandName(), plus a Design copyright brineajay credit line

Dialog surface painted by the .pt-modal class instead of a twin.macro bg-neutral-800. A colour inside a twin.macro css prop is inlined at build time, and below Tailwind 3.1 this config bakes literal hex, which pinned every dialog to the default violet on the black/amber palettes. Same props, exports and portal as stock

Replaces the stock loading ring: caps every size at 22px (stock large was 64px with m-20 of dead margin) and re-asserts border-radius 50% with !important, which the theme's universal `* { border-radius: 0 !important; }` square-corner reset otherwise flattened into a box. Ring colour follows --pt-gold-500
Sharp 3px buttons with uppercase letter-spaced labels

The status block at the top of a server page: the Software and Version rows, the full-width status bar, and the power controls. The order is NOT the reference's and the file docblock says why - software/version first because they are what an OWNER checks and both carry an action; the address moved DOWN beside the console because it is what a PLAYER needs and the player is reading console output; and there is no Connect button, because Aternos's opens a launcher dialog and nothing on this panel does. All four power signals share ONE button class: Start, Stop, Restart and Kill were a large Start with two small square icons beside it, and two sizes read as two different classes of action when they are the same class. Colour carries the difference instead - green start, red stop/kill, blue restart - so the shape stays uniform, and they wrap rather than scroll because a power control you have to scroll sideways to find is one you do not use. Each Change button is rendered only where it leads somewhere: Software is an egg change and this panel's updateBuild takes allocations and limits and no egg_id, so it is an admin action, the button appears for a root admin pointing at the admin Software tab, and for anyone else there is no button at all. Version's Change points at the panel's own Startup page, which is genuinely where a user changes those values. A dead button is the same failure as the 'No egg assigned' string this theme shipped once. The egg name comes from GET /auth/servers/eggs because the panel's server payload carries no egg name at all, and a failure leaves the row on its fallback rather than taking the page down. Power goes over the ServerContext socket with socket.send('set state', ...) exactly as the panel's own PowerButtons does, because the socket is already open here carrying the resource stats and an HTTP call would be a second channel to the same daemon

The console, under the status panel. The header is a plain label strip (`.pt-console-sub`) rather than a card: the power controls and the status chip MOVED into ServerStatusPanel above, because the reference has one large Start that both states the server's condition and offers to change it - a chip plus a row of buttons told the same thing twice - and two stacked dark islands with a gap between them read as one broken island. The ADDRESS came down here too, as a row above the terminal beside ServerDetailsBlock (which carries uptime, CPU, memory, disk and network): one is where you connect, the other is how the thing is doing. It used to sit at the very top of the page as a heading, which is the one place nobody looks while reading console output. PowerButtons is kept and still used elsewhere in the panel; nothing was deleted
Marks the Start button for the gold call-to-action treatment

Terminal chrome: window bar, dots, title and command hint, plus a ResizeObserver on the terminal host so the FitAddon re-fits when the box changes width without a window resize - the mobile drawer opening, or the browser URL bar collapsing

Navy-black terminal, neutral stat cards and gold accents. The mobile full-bleed hack (-ml-4 with width: calc(100% + 2rem)) is gone: it made xterm measure a box 2rem wider than the visible area, so the right end of every line was clipped. Edge-to-edge is kept by zeroing the container padding on phones instead, which does not lie to the measurer. Shadows and transitions use the shared --pt-shadow-* / --pt-dur-* scale
Console detail stat blocks re-skinned to neutral cards with gold icons
Resolves chart palette through ptColor()
Resolves chart grid/tick/line colours through ptColor()
Toolbar layout and branded empty state
Navy path bar with gold links and monospaced type
Card-style file rows with icon tiles, size and modified columns

File manager row, tile, empty-state and mass-action styles. The row deliberately does not set overflow: hidden - it has a square corner radius so nothing needs clipping, and clipping was swallowing the per-row dropdown anchored to it. Uses the shared --pt-shadow-md and --pt-hairline
Branded selection bar with selection counter

Admin -> Site Settings: site name, icon (uploaded file or pasted link), the two background slots (auth/dashboard - upload or pasted link, each with an on/off switch, its own Save button and a black overlay intensity slider), the panel palette picker (default/black/amber) and the Home/Discord/Status quick links. Uploads are capped to what this server can actually accept: php.ini upload_max_filesize/post_max_size are read and the lower of those and the theme cap is what the page advertises, and a file PHP discarded is reported with the reason from the upload error code instead of being treated as "no file chosen". Uploads stored under a fixed stem with a per-upload extension replace EVERY match (deleteStem) rather than the first glob hit, and each read picks the newest file rather than whatever order the filesystem returned - otherwise one failed delete left a stale file that won the next glob and came back on screen

Responsive Site Settings page with server-rendered tabs (no tab JS): General (name + icon with preview, then a separate Login & register and Dashboard background block each with upload/link, on-off switch, intensity slider, live preview and its own Save), Theme (palette cards with colour swatches, validated server-side against a whitelist) and Links (Home/Discord/Status, each with a switch and URL). Upload help text shows the server-derived ceiling rather than the theme cap, so it cannot promise a size PHP will drop. Preview script is vanilla and inlined at the end of @section('content') so it cannot replace the layout's footer-scripts block
POST /auth/register - creates the account directly with the panel's own UserCreationService (hashed password, welcome e-mail, no API key)
Admin -> Registration: enable/disable public sign-up
Registration settings page with the enable switch

Google and Discord sign-in, written directly against each provider's OAuth2 authorization-code flow with Laravel's built-in Http client. NO laravel/socialite and NO composer.json change: the panel does not ship Socialite, and a theme installable only by mutating the host's dependency tree breaks on the next panel upgrade, so the flow is spelled out here using guzzle, the session and Crypt, all of which already ship. The security-relevant decisions, in the order they matter: (1) a per-attempt random `state` is parked in the session, compared with hash_equals and PULLED, so a callback URL cannot be replayed and an attacker cannot feed a victim a code of their own; (2) the provider name is checked against a hardcoded whitelist before any URL is built, so there is no SSRF surface; (3) email_verified (Google) / verified (Discord) is REQUIRED, because matching on a verified address is the entire basis for deciding whose account gets opened; (4) the client secret is encrypted with the panel's APP_KEY on the way into the settings table, since it is a live credential for the admin's own application and the settings table is plain text; (5) the session id is regenerated before login, because the browser carries one pre-auth cookie through the whole round trip. Both exchangeCode() and createFromProfile() return {token}/{user} or {error} rather than a nullable, precisely because a token IS a string and is_string() would have read every success as a failure. Accounts with 2FA are refused rather than signed in - the panel's checkpoint needs a token only the stock password path mints, and quietly bypassing a factor the user enabled would make social login a way around it. A new account is only created while Admin -> Registration is on, so a closed panel is genuinely closed. A successful sign-in also records the provider in the SESSION (SESSION_PROVIDER_KEY, read by the static sessionProvider()), which is what keeps a provider session out of anything that asks for a password - changing the email address today. Session state and not account state on purpose: an account can be signed in with a password in one tab and with Google in another, and only the session knows which is which. It is not the enforcement either - 'remember me' reopens a session from the remember cookie with a fresh session store, so the marker can be absent on a social user - and that is fine, because a provider-created account holds a 48-character random password nobody was told and the password check refuses it regardless. The marker's job is to let the page say WHY rather than failing on a password the user was never given

GET /auth/social/{provider}/redirect and /callback - the two ends of the flow. Both are server-side redirects and neither renders a view: a provider redirects the browser to a URL registered in advance, so the callback cannot be a React route. Failures redirect to the login form with ?social_error= and ?social_message= rather than a session flash, because the panel's flash system only serialises a fixed set of types and an invented one would be dropped

Admin -> Social Login: the OAuth2 client id and secret for Google and Discord, plus a per-provider switch and a clear-secret action. The secret is never rendered back - a blank field means keep the current one, since that is the one field the admin cannot read - and erasure needs its own endpoint because 'blank means unchanged' would otherwise make it unreachable. Enabling a provider with no credentials is allowed and shows as NEEDS CREDENTIALS, which is useful when the application is still being set up in another tab, and renders no button on the login screen until it is complete. The submitted values are read with the request's input() accessor and NOT out of validate(): Laravel's validated() re-inserts each value with Arr::set(), so a dotted rule comes back NESTED as ['google']['client_id'], and reading the dotted key on the returned array always missed - the client id and secret were silently never written while the switch, which reads the request directly, saved fine. That produced a page that looked like it saved, reported 'ON, NOT READY', and dropped the credentials on reload

Social Login settings page: a card per provider with the switch, client id, client secret, and the exact callback URL to paste into the provider console, copyable. The callback URL is the single most common cause of a social login that looks broken and is not, so it is shown rather than documented. The clear-secret forms sit outside the save form because a form cannot nest inside another

The row of social sign-in buttons, or null when no provider is configured. Plain anchors, not buttons with onClick: the flow is server-side redirects, so there is nothing to do in JavaScript, and an anchor keeps middle-click, open-in-new-tab and copy-link working. Both marks are inlined SVG - the panel ships only free-solid-svg-icons, so the Google and Discord brand marks are not available as dependencies and the theme does not add one for two buttons. Google keeps its four colours because their brand rules require the full mark on a light background; Discord is currentColor because their rules permit recolouring on light

Exposes SiteConfiguration.logo / .registration.enabled / .backgrounds / .overlay / .links / .social.providers / .theme.variant; validates link targets and the palette slug server-side against a whitelist; reports recaptcha as disabled so the widget never renders and the exhausted-quota lockout cannot happen. Uploaded images are resolved newest-first and carry their mtime as a ?v= cache-buster - a URL that does not change when the file does is one the browser will not refetch, which is why replacing the favicon used to leave the previous image on screen. .social.providers carries an id and a label only, and lists a provider only when it is both enabled and completely configured, so the client cannot render a button that cannot finish a flow. Adds .account.can_change_email / .signed_in_with, decided from the session SocialAuthService marked on a social sign-in: false for a guest, and false for a provider session. It draws the button and nothing more - the endpoint behind it re-checks all of it - and the failure default is the closed one, because this composer runs on every view in the panel and a missing affordance is a far better failure than a 500. The lookup is wrapped in try/catch because this composer runs on every view in the panel and a settings read that threw would take down unrelated pages

Stock auth routes + GET/POST /auth/register, throttled; drops the stock recaptcha middleware, which would reject every login with HTTP 400 once the shared public keys exhaust their quota. Also GET /auth/social/{provider}/redirect and /callback, with the provider segment constrained to google|discord and outside the throttle group on purpose: the callback is where a visitor lands after an unknown amount of time on the provider's consent screen, and throttling it would hand lockouts to people who did nothing wrong. Adds PUT /auth/account/email (see AccountEmailController) with the same withoutMiddleware('guest') + middleware('auth') pair the logout route uses, because this whole file is mounted inside the panel's guest group and would otherwise bounce a signed-in user away. It is deliberately OUTSIDE throttle:authentication - ten requests a minute across every auth action is the wrong shape for an endpoint allowed three calls a DAY - and takes the panel's own daily email budget inside the controller instead. Also GET /auth/servers/eggs (see ServerEggController), under Auth for the same structural reason: this is the one web route file the theme ships that a normal user can reach, since admin.php is behind AdminAuthenticate and base.php / api-client.php are panel files it does not ship

Stock routes + /admin/site-settings + /admin/registration + /admin/social-auth + GET/POST /admin/servers/view/{server}/software. The social-auth group inherits the panel's own admin middleware from this file's mount, so the root-admin gate is not hand-rolled

Stock admin layout + Site Settings, Registration and Social Login menu items. Favicon handling is kept identical to templates/wrapper.blade.php: newest match wins, mtime cache-buster, MIME type from the extension

Jar installer API, shared by both flavours. Modrinth catalog (search + versions) called straight from the browser - api.modrinth.com sends access-control-allow-origin: *, and Spigot/Hangar do not, so supporting them would mean the panel proxying arbitrary URLs. Installs go through the panel own POST files/pull, which hands the URL to the daemon, so the jar never passes through the browser and needs no new route or permission. JAR_KINDS holds the per-flavour directory, Modrinth project_type and loaders

Classifies a server from its egg variables. The egg name is not exposed to the client - ServerController::index never calls parseIncludes() and egg_features is identical across the Minecraft eggs - but EggVariableTransformer throws on anything not user_viewable, so the variable NAMES that reach the browser are a reliable family fingerprint. Also decides which jar flavours are worth probing, exports serverFamilyLabel() so the card can print a truthful fallback, and serverVersionLabel() so the server page can fill its Version row - it reads serverValue before defaultValue, the way the panel itself resolves a variable, and skips blank values so an egg whose only version variable is empty reports nothing rather than nothing-looking

The Plugins and Mods page - one component, parameterised by JarKind, since installing a Bukkit plugin and a Forge mod are the same operation with a different directory, project type and loaders. Installed list with remove, Modrinth search with a version picker, install, live search, 20-per-page pager, and a warning when a version declares required dependencies. Installing needs file.create, removing file.delete, opening the page file.read

Plugins and Mods page styling on the theme tokens - square corners, gray-700 surfaces, 400 for hairlines and 300 for text, since 600 is the muted fill step and 700+ are surfaces. Uses the shared --pt-shadow-md and --pt-hairline

The software (egg) switch, which this panel has had removed entirely - updateBuild takes only allocations and limits, BuildModificationService handles no egg_id or image, and the admin build view never mentions an egg, so this is written from scratch. Two schema differences from stock Pterodactyl matter: the column is eggs.startup not eggs.start, and there is no eggs.docker_image - this is a Blueprint panel with a docker_images map of {label: image}, so resolveImage keeps the server on the Java version it already has. Rebuilds server_variables from the target egg, carrying values across wherever env_variable exists on both. Refuses while the server is live, reading the power state from the daemon because servers.status never records running

Admin -> Servers -> View -> Software. Root-admin only, but by the panel own gate rather than a check of ours: the routes live in routes/admin.php, which the panel loads inside AdminAuthenticate, and that throws unless root_admin is set. Lists the panel own eggs grouped by nest - no hardcoded list, so imported eggs such as Spigot, Velocity or Fabric appear once an admin adds them

The Software page. Same-family targets (Paper/Spigot/Purpur) and cross-family ones (anything that needs a reinstall) are in separate columns so it is obvious which is which before submitting. Works without JavaScript - the wipe confirmation is enforced server-side - and the script only adds a live summary and the enable/disable. The egg grouping is applied through an explicit if rather than a ${$bucket} variable-variable: that syntax is a PARSE error on PHP 8.2 and later, and Blade passes it through untouched because it is not a Blade construct, so the whole page died before it rendered. That shipped broken once too - php -l on a .blade.php file cannot catch either of these two, which is why the Verification section now compiles every template and lints the OUTPUT

The server-view tab bar, with a Software tab added between Startup and Database. A copy of the panel partial plus that one entry, because the tab bar is shared by every server sub-page and the theme already replaces other shared panel files. Uses Blade's @php/@endphp rather than the stock raw <?php ... ?> block: mixing the two is a 500 on EVERY /admin/servers/view page, since Blade only rewrites an @php/@endphp pair and a lone @endphp passes straight through into markup, while the raw <?php on the first line really does open a PHP block that then runs into the div tag below it, and PHP died on its class attribute. That shipped broken once - see the README's Verification section
